classified.text: An operator shall be able to register a new IoT device by providing a unique identifier, metadata, and authentication credentials.
The platform shall validate device registration data against the schema and reject duplicate identifiers.
SensorGrid shall ingest telemetry streams from registered devices at a rate of up to one million events per second.
The system shall assign a timestamp to each incoming telemetry point using the device's clock or a server‑time fallback.
Users can view a real‑time dashboard that refreshes at least every five seconds with the latest telemetry values per device.
An operator shall be able to create, edit, and delete custom visual widgets on the dashboard.
The platform shall allow operators to define alerting rules based on threshold, rate‑of‑change, or pattern conditions over telemetry streams.
When an alert condition is met, the system shall generate a notification via email, SMS, or webhook within thirty seconds.
Operators shall be able to send command messages to a specific device, with guaranteed delivery acknowledgment.
The system shall queue command messages for offline devices and deliver them when the device reconnects.
An operator shall be able to upload a firmware package and initiate a staged rollout to a selected device group.
SensorGrid shall report the status of each firmware update (pending, in‑progress, succeeded, failed) per device.
The platform shall retain raw telemetry for a configurable retention period (minimum thirty days) and automatically roll up data into hourly and daily aggregates.
Users can query historical time‑series data with a time‑range filter and receive results in JSON or CSV format.
The system shall support ad‑hoc aggregation queries (average, min, max, percentile) over any retained time window.
An administrator shall be able to assign role‑based access permissions to operators for device groups and dashboards.
The platform shall enforce mutual TLS authentication for all device‑to‑cloud connections.
Users can export dashboard configurations and import them into another SensorGrid instance.
The system shall provide a health‑check endpoint that reports ingestion latency, storage utilization, and alerting status.
An operator shall be able to tag devices with arbitrary key‑value pairs and filter views by tags.
SensorGrid shall support schema‑versioned telemetry, allowing devices to evolve payload structures without breaking existing queries.
The platform shall log every command transmission, firmware update, and alert event with immutable audit records.
The platform shall scale horizontally to handle a two‑fold increase in ingestion throughput without degradation of latency.
System shall maintain end‑to‑end ingestion latency below two hundred milliseconds for ninety‑nine point nine percent of telemetry points.
SensorGrid shall achieve ninety‑nine point nine‑five percent monthly availability, with automatic failover across availability zones.
All stored telemetry shall be encrypted at rest using AES‑256 and in transit using TLS 1.3.
The platform shall implement role‑based access control (RBAC) and immutable audit logging to satisfy compliance requirements.
System shall expose Prometheus‑compatible metrics for CPU, memory, request rates, and error counts.
The deployment shall be containerized and orchestrated via Kubernetes, supporting rolling updates with zero‑downtime.
The platform shall retain historical data for the configured period while ensuring storage cost does not exceed $0.02 per GB‑month.
SensorGrid shall automatically rebalance streaming partitions to prevent hot spots.
The system shall provide API rate limiting per tenant to protect against abusive usage.
